entry.title: My current and upcoming personal projects
entry.content:
These are my current in-flight or about-to-start personal little projects:

  • This blog (in progress) — I’ve been successfully maintaining this blog for over 3 months now, so I guess it ought to be reclassified as a “hobby” rather than a project by now ☺️

  • 14-day uniform (in progress) — I’m rebooting my wardrobe for autumn, adding a few more muted colours to the mainly black pieces I’m wearing now, while keeping quantities down and keeping things relaxed and very casual.

  • Lose weight (to do) — Due to some comfort eating, I’ve put on a few kilos and am getting close to 25 in BMI. Time to bring it back down to 23! It always used to be easy for me to lose weight — I’d just skip biscuits for a while — but it’s getting harder and harder these days, so this time it will no doubt take a bit more effort and dedication.

  • Create the perfect toolbox (to do) — Good tools make everything a lot easier, so when we finally move into our new apartment, I want to do so equipped with a new toolbox filled with good versions of all the tools I need.

  • EDC reboot (to do) — I keep carrying my old, almost empty backpack around every day, as my umbrella won’t fit in my small bag. I want to get a sling bag just big enough to fit a brolly and an iPad, like the Aer Day Sling Max, and then curate a few more bits and bobs to go in it.

  • Figure out my career path (in progress) — I’m in a good job with a good employer and have no plan going anywhere, but nevertheless, I need to keep an eye on my future employability. The kind of roles I used to do seem to have all but disappeared, so I need to make sure I build towards something that’s a bit more sought after these days.

entry.title: My honest and somewhat nitpicky review of Apple Watch Series 11
entry.content:
I would love to just have a good old Casio watch, but there are two reasons why I have a smartwatch instead:

  1. I need a silent alarm to wake me up in the morning without waking my husband.
  2. I want a step counter that counts every step instead of just those when I carry my phone so that the number looks higher.

For many years, I had a Fitbit. It did these two things very well, and I was happy.

But then four events roughly coincided in time. Firstly, Google bought Fitbit and demanded to get all my data. Secondly, I bought an iPhone Pro Max, thinking the bigger screen would make reading more pleasant than a normal-sized phone. Thirdly, London became the phone theft capital of the world and I started worrying about having my phone snatched when taking it out to skip the ads in the podcast I was listening to, or whatever. And lastly, I went to Korea and was able to buy an Apple Watch on the cheep.

That was why I decided to get an Apple Watch. I wanted a non-Google, phone-snatching-preventing iPhone remote at a discount.

I have now had my Apple Watch Series 11 for 10 months and feel there are a few things I want to get off my chest, so here’s a very honest review.

entry.title: How I budget
entry.content:
When it comes to finances, I subscribe to the idea that automation is how to make it easy to stay on top of things. I just don’t have the will to track every expense or go through account statements.

Over time, I have fine-tuned a system that I find makes it really easy for me to stay on top of things without thinking, avoiding my expenses ballooning or me wondering at the end of the month where all the money went.

The main ideas are:

  1. Use a joint account for joint expenses, and joint expenses only
  2. Pay myself a monthly allowance for everyday spending
  3. Automated, simple investments
  4. Save for big expenses
  5. Give a little bit to charity

entry.title: Thoughts on the blog so far
entry.content:
I’m happy to see how this blog project seems to be surviving so far, two and a half months in.

The whole thing started as an impulse and an AI prompt about me missing personal blogs and when the Internet was free from slop and ads.

The AI helped me build the platform, and I have semi-regularly been filling it with short journal posts, photos and random thoughts. This is the 44th post, excluding the very shortest notes.

I haven’t actually shared the blog address with anyone and the traffic is very low. Tbh, that’s quite liberating! I can post whatever I feel like, without worrying about whether anyone will find it interesting or whether it is “on brand” or whatever.

Because that’s the whole point of this blog. It’s mine. It’s a manually curated feed of my life and interests. By me, for me. There are no retweets and no like button for anyone to press and no sense of failure when they don’t.

It’s just me putting my notes on my wall. If anyone happens to walk past and see them, that’s cool, but it’s not the main purpose.

entry.title: My wish list (August 2026)
entry.content:
My wish list is a list of the things I crave, but I put off buying. Maybe they are a bit on the expensive side, or I’m not sure whether the desire will blow over. Or I’m just savouring the anticipation.

Here’s the current list:

  • TOYO Cantilever Toolbox ST-350 MG (Moss Green)
    One of the things I want to do when I move next is to put together a well-thought-through toolbox, instead of the random bits and bobs I’ve accumulated over the years. The first step is, of course, the toolbox itself, and TOYO make the best one, imho.

  • Apple AirPods Max 2 (Midnight)
    My noise-cancelling over-ear Bose headphones have ended up in the office, and the in-ear AirPods replacing them at home and out and about are not isolating enough when I travel or when the husband is taking work meetings at home.

  • Lego The Endurance
    I was a massive Lego fan as a kid, and I still am, even if I’m a rather infrequent builder these days. The last time was a bonsai tree for my desk at work, but now I have my eyes set on a nice-looking ship model for my desk at home, once I move.

  • Carhartt WIP dungarees (black rinsed)
    I’ve always had a thing for dungarees. I really like the look of them on top of a hoodie or a white tee. Right now, though, the pair I have aren’t getting much wear, so I think it would be a good move to get a pair of my favourite black Carhartt WIP dungarees instead.

  • The future model of iPad Mini
    For many years, I didn’t have a laptop and just used an iPad for everything. I do love the MacBook Air that eventually replaced it, but there are times when I miss the iPad’s simplicity. Not least in my EDC, so I don’t have to wear my backpack. I’m therefore quite tempted to get an iPad Mini, but the current model feels a bit old, so I’m waiting to see what happens.

entry.title: A recap of the summer so far ☀️
entry.content:
This blog has been running for just over 2 months now, so I figured it might make sense to post a recap of what’s been going on. Mainly for my own benefit, but you’re welcome to read along!

  • The biggest event of the summer so far was definitely moving house, from our home of many years to a temporary flat further east, bringing with it new views and a new commute.

  • Travel has been limited to a day trip to Brighton and 2 weeks in Sweden for holiday and remote working, with an enjoyable trip to the island Klädesholmen up the coast, as well as a bit of boating.

  • Culturally, it’s been a pretty decent period. I’ve been to V&A East, The Serpentine Pavilion, Tate modern, Pilane Sculpture Park in Sweden, The Royal Academy Summer Exhibition, NIGO at the Design Museum, The Quentin Blake Centre for Illustration and Anish Kapoor at Hayward Gallery. I’ve also attended two Proms at Royal Albert Hall.

  • Personal projects have obviously involved the blog itself, which I launched on 24 May, using AI to build my own static site generator. I’ve also been playing around with creating some signal flag icons as well as a rainbow blow logo for a different kind of signalling. I also started a reboot of my wardrobe, which I need to get back to.

  • Life stuff hasn’t been too dramatic, but I did a write-up of my values as well as a life-tracker to keep my focus. My birthday is coming up, so it’s likely I will soon start creating a plan for what my next year might look like.

  • Financially, I’ve been getting used to the higher expenses in the new place, including a hike in travel costs.

  • What I bought has been limited to day-to-day items, with nothing new or exciting to report, except for one thing I will post about when it arrives.

  • Most unexpected has been the weather. Where’s the rain gone? And it’s been hot pretty much every day. I feel ready for autumn!

All in all, so far, so good! 😊
